newsitem.title: USA: Ex Bankers Trust VP charged with insider trading.
newsitem.headline: Ex Bankers Trust VP charged with insider trading.

text.p: A former vice president for compliance with Bankers Trust Co. and its broker-dealer unit BT Securities Corp. was arrested Wednesday for insider trading, federal prosecutors said.

Former Bankers Trust executive Alan Stricoff of Plainview, N.Y., was charged with passing confidential information about ITT Corp.'s 1994 acquisition of Caesars World Inc. that he learned from his employer.
He was arrested along with his brother Jeffrey Stricoff, of Syossett, N.Y, who owns a Manhattan art gallery.
If convicted, the brothers each face a possible maximum sentence of 15 years in prison and a $1.25 million fine.
The complaint filed in federal court in Manhattan alleged that Jeffrey Stricoff used the inside information to buy Caesars World options.

It alleges that Alan Stricoff's job responsibilities included reviewing Bankers Trust compliance with federal securities laws. Because of this he had access to a list of companies that Bankers Trust had acquired "inside" information about through its investment, banking, corporate finance or other business activities.
Alan Stricoff allegedly passed insider information about five companies, including Caesars World, to his brother and two others.
Bankers Trust was involved in the takeover because ITT had approached it to serve as financial adviser.

The complaint alleged Alan Stricoff and a co-conspirator had obtained inside information about the Caesar's World acquisition at a meeting in which Bankers Trust compliance personnel were instructed to closely monitor trading in the securities of ITT and Caesars World.
Bankers Trust now operates under the name Bankers Trust New York Corp.
